content.text: My DashboardQuizzesMy SchoolsSchools You Might Also LikeCompare SchoolsMy ScholarshipsReading ListAdviceGet PremiumArizona State University Tuition & Financial AidArizona State University's tuition is $12,975 for in-state and $35,167 for out-of-state students. Compared with the national average cost of in-state tuition of $12,436, Arizona State University is more expensive. For students coming from out of state, the tuition is more expensive than the national average cost of out-of-state tuition of $29,815.These figures include both tuition and fees, also referred to as the sticker price. Fees differ by institution and may fund library services, student gym facilities, student centers, technology resources and campus health centers.As you’re comparing costs of different institutions, also consider the total cost and the net price. The total cost is the sticker price, plus the cost of food and housing, books and supplies, and transportation and personal expenses. At Arizona State University, the total cost is $34,175 for in-state students and $55,091 for out-of-state students. The net price is the average cost of the university after aid and scholarship funds are discounted from the total cost, which come in on average at $26,405 for in-state students and $51,356 for out-of-state students receiving need-based aid.My Fit ScoreMy Fit Custom College Ranking Does this school fit your college needs? autopayShow MoreFinancial Aid Statistics for Arizona State UniversityFinancial aid refers to funding that students can use to pay for college and is generally awarded based on need or merit.Need-based aid is determined by your or your family’s demonstrated ability to pay for college, as calculated by the Free Application for Federal Student Aid, known as the FAFSA. The average need-based scholarship or grant awarded to first-year students at Arizona State University was $15,976. Additionally, 55% of first-year students received need-based financial aid in fall 2023.Need-based self-help aid includes federal loans and work-study. The average need-based self-help aid awarded to first-year students was $3,206.Merit-based aid, also called non-need-based aid, is awarded for a specific talent or academic achievement. The average non-need-based scholarship or grant awarded to first-year students at Arizona State University – excluding any athletic scholarships, if applicable – was $10,179.Arizona State University met 57% of its students’ financial aid need. The median monthly federal loan payment (if it were repaid over 10 years at 5.05% interest) for student federal loan borrowers who graduated is $207.Additionally, 7% of graduating students at Arizona State University took out private loans.
